judgments.fix: each emission the ring accepts allocates a fresh copy of the ring (the CAS handoff's value semantics), so a noisy frame allocates up to sixteen rings of growing length per writer
judgments.backing_entry: D-136 (restated in D-369 and spec §11.8, spec.md:9662-9664)
judgments.note: The DiagBatch docstring (src/dataplane.jl:100-103) states the copy-on-append choice, so the copy is deliberate. Nothing in the log or pending records it. The alternative fix is code that appends in place to a ring allocated once per frame.

judgments.evidence: Probe: past the ring, emissions 17 to 20 allocated 0 bytes, so the integer-increment half holds. Up to the bound, sixteen ring copies of lengths 1 to 16 were allocated (about 5.6 KB), not one ring of 16 (src/dataplane.jl:144-145).
judgments.fix: the worst case per writer per boundary is sixteen ring copies of growing length, the last holding sixteen values, and everything past the ring is an integer increment

notes: I verified all 42 claims at W = d7d3ddff and modified no tracked file. The probe is at /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/L9a_v/probe.jl and I ran it twice; the first run failed on a missing Logging import, which I fixed. Every claim is a log entry. Under log_rules.md rules 1 and 2, a drift fix lands as an annotation or a superseding note, not as a rewrite of the old prose. The fix texts give the current fact. The two deviations of substance are L9a-092 and L9a-093: the diagnostic ring is copied at every accepted emission (16 copies of growing length, about 5.6 KB per noisy writer per frame), while D-136, D-369 and spec §11.8 promise one lazily allocated ring of 16. L9a-067 is a smaller deviation: an activation entry holds no compiled plans and no validated flag, and spec §9.4 at spec.md:5767 still says it does.
